root_cause_label: Insufficient CoreWars domain expertise to design competitive warrior
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent lacked the CoreWars domain expertise needed to design a warrior meeting all win-rate thresholds, cycling through elementary textbook patterns (scanner, replicator, dwarf bomber) across 170+ iterations without converging on a competitive strategy, and at the final step its file-write sequence left stale content (the original Hybrid Warrior) in my_warrior.red instead of the intended Dwarf Bomber.
t_err_evidence: From step 1 the agent proceeds with elementary CoreWars strategies (scan-and-bomb, simple replicators, dwarf bomber) without any domain knowledge about competitive warrior design techniques such as clear-gate defense, imp-spiral resistance, or p-space bootstrapping; this gap ensures no design it can produce will meet all required win-rate thresholds.
t_commit_evidence: At step 44 the agent explicitly acknowledges that the first complete warrior design fails all opponents except Stone (80%) and starts a third redesign with no new domain insight; from this point every subsequent attempt recycles the same elementary strategies and never converges, making failure inevitable given the agent's actual behavior.
t_surface_evidence: Step 25: the first battle test shows 'Results: 0 10 0' (zero wins vs Stone), and steps 42-43 confirm zero wins against Snake and G2-Clear, providing clear observable evidence that the warrior designs are not competitive.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain knowledge about CoreWars competitive warrior design; it knows only textbook primitives (scan ADD+CMP+JMP, SPL/DAT bomb, MOV.I replicator) but not the advanced techniques (adaptive clear routines, anti-vampire defenses, p-space switching, or the specific step-size tuning) required to beat a diverse set of sophisticated opponents simultaneously.
forewarning_evidence: Step 25 shows 'Results: 0 10 0' (Hybrid Warrior loses all 10 rounds vs Stone). Steps 40, 42, 43 show poor results against Paper (0/10), Snake (0/9), G2-Clear (0/6). The repeated pattern of losing 0 rounds (or near-zero) against the same opponents across multiple redesigns is a consistent forewarning before t_commit=44.
